item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Nov 15, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Above Bone — Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. The forms are camouflaged, as if growing from or being returned to the ground. Layered colorful patterns, resists, and luster build up over multiple firings. Pat

item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. item.title: Mean Girls The Musical — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
November 6 through November 29, 2026 Cady Heron may have grown up on an African savanna, but nothing prepared her for the wild and vicious ways of her strange new home: suburban Illinois. How will this naïve newbie rise to the top of the popularity pecking order? By taking on The Plastics, a trio of lionized frenemies led by the charming but ruthless Regina George. But when Cady and her friends devise a “Revenge Party” to end Regina’s reign, she learns the hard way that you can’t cross a queen bee without getting stung. Recommended for ages 13 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Pamela Trokanski Dance Theatre 2026 Fall Concert - Walking Contradictions — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM — Louise H Kellogg Memorial Theater at the Pamela Trokanski Dance Workshop
item.description:
The Pamela Trokanski Dance Theatre invites the community to join them for the premiere of their Fall Concert: Walking Contradictions, a thoughtful, and sometimes humorous exploration of our lives as asymmetrical beings, finding beauty in the balance of symmetry but at the same time seemingly unable to escape what is unbalanced, whether that is in ourselves, our communities, or in how we behave in the world around us. Joining the PTDT are the PTDT Apprentice Company, Light Ballet Company, and The Third Stage. Known for work that integrates a strong sense of athleticism and technical training with idiosyncratic movements and a diverse range of movers, including dancers ranging in age from 10 to 90+, this is not your average dance performance! Tickets are available in advance and at the door. General Admission – $20 Children, Students, and Adults 65+ – $15 (A 4% surcharge is added to all electronic payments)
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Women's Circles (Mom Anger and Rage) — Sun Nov 15, 3:00 PM — 1550 Cannery Ave
item.description:
Davis Women’s Circles are made for all mamas, including pregnant ones! Held in a beautiful, uplifting and safe space, you get to reset, connect, and discover what mothering on your own terms looks like. This special mini-retreat focuses on the common experience of mom anger and rage. This circle is open to any mama who experiences anger/rage or is simply interested in the topic. We’ll be cultivating understanding, empathy and greater self-compassion and also discuss helpful tools. It includes relevant activities, connecting with amazing local mamas and tasty bites. Pre-purchase your ticket, $38 (https://tocarrywonder.com/davis-womens-circles/). Sliding-scale tickets available.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest — Sun Nov 15, 7:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest returns to the Davis Odd Fellows Hall for a three-week run starting Sunday, November 1st. The genre for this series of films is Screwball Comedies of the 1960s & 1970s. Everyone is welcome to enjoy these films. Doors open at 6:29 p.m. and the films start at 7:01 p.m.Popcorn is provided free of charge. The bar will be open to purchase beer, wine, or soft drinks. Davis Enterprise Film Critic/Reviewer Derrick Bang will give a short talk before each movie about interesting details on the plot, director, actors, and fun things to look for while watching. He’ll do a quick Q&A afterwards. According to Bazooka will play before each movie. November 1st we kick off with “One, Two, Three” a 1961 American political comedy film directed by Billy Wilder and written by Wilder and I. A. L. Diamond. This film stars James Cagney, Horst Buchholz, and Arlene Francis. November 8th we bring you Mel Brooks’1968 comedy, “The Producers” starring Zero Mostel and Gene Wild

Tuesday, Nov. 17 as part of the Department of Art and Art History’s public programming — made possible in part by a Maria Manetti Shrem Endowed Chair in Art Studio. item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Wed Dec 2, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 28, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No
